one_month_reasoning: No Nebius earnings fall inside the window: Q3-26 results are expected around 2026-11-10 (third-party estimate; the Q3-25 report came in mid-November), so the report and the promised formal 2027 guidance most likely land after Oct 31. Events inside the window are second-hand: hyperscaler Q3 earnings and capex commentary (MSFT/META/GOOGL/AMZN, late October), which move AI-infrastructure names both ways, plus ongoing supply of stock (Form 144 filings in Aug-Sep, an open ATM program with ~12M shares left at 6/30, and holders of the ~15.8M shares from the August note exchange who may sell or hedge). The 10-yr Treasury rising to 5.29% is a mild headwind for long-duration names. The Inferize deal (Oct 1) and the Palantir partnership (Sep 8) are already in the price. With no company-specific catalyst I stay close to a symmetric distribution around $232 at about 29% monthly vol (106%/3.5 ≈ 30%), with a median of about $231 that leans very slightly lower for supply and rates.

fair_value.method: Blend of a capacity-driven DCF (40%, $88/share probability-weighted across bear/base/bull, WACC 13.5%, 3% terminal growth) and EV/NTM sales at Oct-2027 (60%, 4.5x on $25B NTM revenue less $16.6B net debt plus $3.65B stakes over 372M diluted shares = $268). Blended 12-month fair value is about $196, roughly 16% below spot.

Long-run nominal growth below the 5.29% risk-free; blended Dutch/US statutory rates (judgment, NOLs ignored for conservatism).

bear.story: AI-capex digestion or GPU price deflation: new-deal ACV per MW falls back toward the $12M 2026 base, capacity slips, and funding of $25-30B/yr of capex leans on dilutive ATM and converts. The market re-rates NBIS to about 2x NTM sales and starts to price DCF-like cash-flow risk; a Redburn-style $84 target becomes the anchor.

base.story: Nebius deploys roughly 0.9-1GW in 2027 and posts 2027 revenue of $13-15B with a YE27 ARR near $20B, adj. EBITDA margin around 50%, and keeps funding capex through prepayments plus secured debt. The multiple compresses to about 4x NTM sales as growth slows, roughly offsetting the growth, so the stock ends near today's level with heavy volatility along the way.

bull.story: Q2-26 deal economics ($20-25M/MW, ~22-month payback) hold across the more than 1GW deployed in 2027, short-term premium deals and auctions lift pricing, Vera Rubin ramps on time, and YE27 ARR exceeds $25B. The market holds 5-6x NTM sales and the late-2026 notes ($313-325 conversion prices) end up in the money.

thesis_break_reason: At about $115 the equity would be worth roughly $43B, or about $50B EV on a diluted basis, under 2x the ~$25B 2027-28 revenue path and below the Sep-2025 convert conversion price ($138.75). Trading there would most likely mean something fundamental broke rather than ordinary volatility: demand or pricing per MW has rolled over, capacity is slipping, or financing has become distressed. That would invalidate the base case of roughly 1GW per year at mid-teens $M/MW.

reasoning: Research came mostly from primary documents: the Q2-26 shareholder letter, the 6-K press release, interim financial statements and OFR, the call transcript, the August convertible 6-Ks, the AGM share count, and the September/October 6-Ks. Key facts: Q2 revenue $582M (+454%), AI cloud adj. EBITDA margin 49.7%, ARR $3.0B, FY26 guide reaffirmed (ARR $7-9B, revenue $3.0-3.4B, ~40% EBITDA margin, capex $20-25B), RPO $37.5B with 36% recognised within 24 months, $8.0B cash at 6/30 plus $5.75B of converts in August, $6.0B deferred revenue, and new deals at $20-25M/MW with ~22-month payback. The share count is about 372M diluted once the in-the-money converts, the NVIDIA warrants and the exchange shares are included. Valuation: a capacity-driven DCF at a 13.5% WACC (rf 5.29%) gives only about $35-87 per share in base cases, because the business must spend $25-30B a year on short-lived GPUs. Only if Q2-26 pricing persists (bull, about $224) does the DCF approach the price, so the probability-weighted DCF is about $88. A market-relative EV/NTM sales check against CoreWeave (4.9x) gives about $268. Blending 40/60 gives a fair value of about $196, which says the stock prices in that new-deal economics persist. Analyst targets ($84-$415, averages $242-$284) show the same two-sided disagreement. Distribution: a scenario mixture (bear $95 / base $225 / bull $400 at 25/50/25, with mean about $236 and median about $215) averaged with a single lognormal (median $215, sigma 0.8), fat-tailed because realized vol is 106% (I used ~80% forward because a large part of 2025-26 vol came from re-rating events). This gives P(≥ today's $232) of 0.46, slightly below a coin flip: the fundamentals argue below spot but the momentum and contracted backlog argue above. Limits: Twelve Data and Alpha Vantage estimate endpoints were unavailable (plan/rate limits), so 2027 consensus revenue and some earlier convert conversion prices come from search snippets, not fetched pages, and Q3 ATM usage is unknown.
